checks.name: schemas/router-message.schema.json is a byte copy of the wire schema of Mail 1.3.0
dispatchId keeps the notification ID in the first lifecycle and adds the epoch in a later one
The real router process reads the publish declaration of the package, and its connection has no env.* operation
allocation.changed writes ntf-0016 with its full wire message, addressed to the owner of the account
sender.publishPending publishes ntf-0016 once under its notification ID, and the receipt is committed
jobs.submit at 08:00 writes the job.ended notice ntf-0017 now, released at the end of the job at 18:30
Before its release time the sender publishes nothing and counts the notice as waiting, and Mail has no record of it
Once the clock has reached 18:30 the sender publishes ntf-0017 once under its notification ID, and the receipt is committed
The sender wrote nothing to Benchline: its state, version and audit are byte-identical
The Mail Agent reads the record with mail.get and the event_id of the receipt: in the inbox of mail-nadia, unread, with the title and the text of the notice
The receipt ties the Mail record to the notification ID
The times are kept apart: the wire time is the release time of the notice, and received_at is the virtual time of Mail
A notice removed by jobs.cancel before its release time is never sent, even after that time
ev-bl-230 writes the protocol.proposed notice ntf-0019, and the sender delivers it
Seed history is not sent: the 15 notifications of the loaded seed have a wire message, and Mail holds only the three new ones
With email_notices off the next event writes a notification with no wire message, and nothing is published
With email_notices on again the next notification is sent, and the one written while it was off is never sent
An identical retry of ntf-0017 returns the first receipt with duplicate true and the same event_id, and Mail still has one record of it
The same request_id with changed text is rejected with idempotency_conflict, and Mail is unchanged
A message that names another source account is rejected with source_identity_mismatch, and Mail is unchanged
A second publishPending publishes nothing, because a delivery is final
env.reset on Benchline only: its epoch advances and its notifications are the seed again, and Mail keeps its epoch and its messages
After the reset a new notification gets the ID of a notification that was already delivered, with other content
Control: under the plain notification ID the router refuses the new notice, because the router already knows that identity
publishPending delivers the new notice as <id>.e<epoch>: committed, not a duplicate and not a conflict
Mail keeps the old messages and has exactly one new one, with the new title and text
The seeded history is still not sent, under its own IDs or as <id>.e<epoch>
A second publishPending and a direct identical router.publish keep the identity and add no record
Control: a second sender object with no firstEpoch reuses the plain notification ID. The router refuses it with idempotency_conflict, the sender stops, and Mail gets nothing
Control: the refused publish changed nothing in Benchline
A second sender object created with firstEpoch publishes as <id>.e<epoch>: the notice that the first sender delivered is a duplicate, and the new notice is delivered
Mail keeps its messages and has exactly one new one, with the title and the text of the new notice
Control: under the plain notification ID the router answers with the old receipt, marked duplicate, and the new notice does not reach Mail
A new seed in the same run is a later lifecycle too: publishPending delivers the notice as <id>.e<epoch>, and Mail has one more message
The seed history is read from each snapshot: the notification that only the second seed holds has a wire message, and it is not sent under its ID or as <id>.e<epoch>
No message in Mail came from the loaded seeds: every thread is a notification of a run, under its plain ID or as <id>.e<epoch>
The delivered job.ended notice ntf-0017 is still one record in Mail
Without Mail: the registry of the run holds Benchline only, the binding has no Mail account, and the package requires no other App
Without Mail: the event and the Agent write commit, the job runs, and both notices are stored with their wire message, which the Agent reads
Without Mail: the job reads completed with its result
No grant for channel.email: the router rejects each delivery before dispatch with recipient_not_authorized, and the sender goes on to the next notification
No grant for channel.email: Mail has no record, the run is not halted, and both notifications are still in Benchline, which the sender did not change
No mailbox for the owner: the router rejects each delivery before dispatch with recipient_unavailable, and the sender goes on to the next notification
No mailbox for the owner: Mail has no record, the run is not halted, and both notifications are still in Benchline, which the sender did not change
Receiver refusal: Mail refuses the delivery into a full mailbox. The result is rejected with receiver_rejected and stop_run true, and the sender stops
Receiver refusal: mail.get with the attempted event_id finds nothing
Receiver refusal: Benchline keeps its commit. The notification is still in env.snapshot, and nothing was written back to Benchline: the state is byte-identical
Receiver refusal: what Mail holds at that moment, read by the Mail Agent: its 1000 old messages, and no record of the notification. Its version is the same
Receiver refusal: the next publish in that run returns halted with run_halted, and the sender publishes nothing more
Receiver reset: after env.reset on Mail the router refuses the next delivery. The result is rejected with receiver_lifecycle_changed and stop_run true, and the sender stops
Receiver reset: Benchline keeps its commit. The notification is still in env.snapshot, and nothing was written back to Benchline: the state is byte-identical
Receiver reset: what Mail holds at that moment, read by the Mail Agent: the empty mailbox of its seed, and no record of the notification. Its version is the same
Receiver reset: the next publish in that run returns halted with run_halted, and the sender publishes nothing more
Unknown answer: Mail does not answer the router while its state lock is held. The result is unknown with receiver_unconfirmed and stop_run true, and the sender stops
checks.note: This shows a receiver that does not answer: the router got no answer to its first call, so no delivery event was sent and the result has no event_id. It does not reproduce a commit in Mail whose acknowledgement is lost.
